description: §19.8.3 handling form 1 (S451 R11) on a cell write in a function (RUNTIME, sqlEngine:"real"): `@c = ?{…}.get() !{…}`. It is the same cell write as the unhandled `@c = ?{…}.get()`: the function is split client/server (§19.9.9), the query runs on the server, and the CLIENT cell receives the row (`notes`), `not` (`empties` — no row is not a failure), or the arm's value when the query fails to run (`gone` is declared but never created → `.QueryFailed` → "failed"). Pre-S455 (g-impl1-handled-sql-lowering-defects-s455 item 2) the guard hid the cell write from route inference: the whole function went to the server, `@c` lowered to a server-side `_scrml_reactive_set` that never reached the client, and every cell stayed "init" at exit 0.
rationale: §19.8.3: "**A `!{}` handler on the query** — written after the terminator (`.get()`, `.all()`, `.run()`), its arms match `SqlError` variants"; "A query that runs and matches nothing succeeds: `.get()` on zero rows returns `not`". The handler adds a failure path; the cell write it guards is unchanged.
